changes.title: posthog-js (184KB) statically imported in root layout â€” ships on first paint of every page, even before consent
changes.evidence: analytics.ts:1 `import posthog from "posthog-js";` is pulled through PostHogProvider.tsx:3 into the root layout (layout.tsx:13, rendered :342). Built chunk f419a0d964ad60bc.js = 184KB is referenced by page + explore client-reference manifests, so it loads on first paint of landing and every 2D surface. Yet initAnalytics() (analytics.ts:29-36) bails unless hasAnalyticsConsent() and skips in native â€” so 184KB is downloaded/parsed and never used for most first paints.
changes.fix: Remove the top-level import. Make initAnalytics() async and, after the consent/native/key guards pass, do `const posthog = (await import("posthog-js")).default;`. Lazy-import in optOutAnalytics() too. Removes 184KB from the shared layout chunk on every first paint.

changes.title: Photos never get a stored thumbnail â€” full-res originals loaded for every wall tile
changes.evidence: On upload only VIDEO/AUDIO thumbs persist (memoryStore.ts:218). UploadPanel only generates a thumb for video/audio (UploadPanel.tsx:111-112). MassImportPanel generates a 200px photo thumb (MassImportPanel.tsx:117) but commitAll() discards it, committing `dataUrl: item.dataUrl` (full-res) with no thumbnailUrl (:227-238). So DB thumbnail_url is null for photos and PhotoWall.tileSources()/MediaThumb fall back to full-res file_url. PhotoWall renders a tile per memory across the whole library ("potentially thousand-tile wall", PhotoWall.tsx:362), each pulling a multi-MB original.
changes.fix: Call generateThumbnail(file,280) for images in UploadPanel.processFile and set mem.thumbnailUrl; in MassImportPanel.commitAll upload item.previewUrl and pass thumbnailUrl into the mem (PhotoWall/MediaThumb already prefer thumbnailUrl, PhotoWall.tsx:32-39). Add a photo variant to useThumbnailBackfill.ts (currently `if (!isVideo) continue;`) to backfill existing photos.

changes.title: 6.5 MB tuscan_landscape_2k.hdr background HDRI downloads on MOBILE despite comment claiming it's skipped
changes.evidence: MOBILE_QUALITY sets `loadBackgroundHDRI: true` (mobilePerf.ts:161). ExteriorScene.tsx:205-206 comment says "Skipped on mobile (6.5 MB)" but the guard `if(Q.loadBackgroundHDRI){loadHDRI(ren,HDRI_TUSCAN_LANDSCAPE)...}` is true on mobile, so phones DO fetch tuscan_landscape_2k.hdr (6,531,494 bytes). Only POTATO_QUALITY (:180) sets it false. Code and comment disagree; mobile pays a 6.5 MB decode on the most common exterior entry.
changes.fix: Set `loadBackgroundHDRI: false` in MOBILE_QUALITY (mobilePerf.ts:161) and rely on the procedural sky sphere â€” or ship a 1k downscaled HDRI for mobile. Cuts ~6.5 MB off mobile exterior entry.

changes.title: 2D Atrium/Library pay full 3D cost: WebGL context + entire ExteriorScene graph built eagerly on app mount
changes.evidence: warmPalaceScene mounts ExteriorScene via portal when `hasVisitedPalace`, which is hard-coded `const hasVisitedPalace = true; // eager mount` (:654). It renders in every navMode branch incl atrium (:1114) and library (:1127); host div created unconditionally (:655-667). ExteriorScene mount creates a WebGLRenderer (ExteriorScene.tsx:186), sky canvas, terrain/grass, HDRIs and PBR textures before the user taps Palace. Render loop is paused but the one-time BUILD + context alloc + downloads still run â€” a user landing on /atrium who never enters still pays full 3D init.
changes.fix: Gate the eager mount: only mount warmPalaceScene once the user has entered 3D at least once this session (or defer via requestIdleCallback after atrium first paint) instead of `const hasVisitedPalace = true`. Keep the warm-persist for palaceâ†”atrium round-trips but don't build WebGL during first atrium/library paint.

changes.title: Full en.json (295KB) bundled into the landing client chunk as a runtime fallback value
changes.evidence: LandingV2Client.tsx:23 `import enMessages from "@/messages/en.json";` is a runtime (not type-only) import of a 295,713-byte file, used at runtime at :435 `default: mod = { default: enMessages };`, so it can't tree-shake. Other locales are correct (dynamic import at :431-434 â†’ separate chunks); only the en default branch leaks the whole file eagerly. Grepping built client chunks for `landingV2` matches 260-300KB chunks.
changes.fix: Dynamically import en to match other locales: `default: mod = await import("@/messages/en.json");`. Change the top-level import to a type alias (`type Messages = typeof import("@/messages/en.json")`) for the `typeof` derivations at :41-44. Removes ~295KB from the landing first-paint chunk.

changes.title: next/image points at auth-required /api/media proxy without unoptimized â€” public images fail to load
changes.evidence: Grid `<Image src={mem.fileUrl!} fill .../>` (:369-376) and detail (:567) use fileUrl = raw DB file_url = `/api/media/memories/{userId}/{file}` (public-share/route.ts:110; upload builds it at api/upload/route.ts:113). That proxy returns 401 with no authenticated user (route.ts:66-68). Unlike LibraryView (which sets `unoptimized`, LibraryView.tsx:3242/3259/2676), PublicGallery doesn't, so Next's optimizer server-fetches the src, gets 401, and the image fails. Even logged-in viewers hit the dynamic proxy with no CDN.
changes.fix: Return a directly-loadable URL from public-share/route.ts (R2/Supabase signed URL) instead of the auth-gated /api/media path, or add a public read path in /api/media for shared memories. Keep next/image pointed at a CDN-cacheable origin.

changes.title: 200 req/min media rate limit can 429 the photo wall on fast scroll, silently dropping images
changes.evidence: `rateLimit("media:${user.id}", 200, 60_000)` â†’ 429 (route.ts:70-73). Every image is served through this force-dynamic proxy (:7; upload returns `/api/media/...`, api/upload/route.ts:113). PhotoWall renders one per memory with lazy load; scrolling 300+ photos fast fires >200 requests/min â†’ 429. On error TileMedia advances sources then MediaThumb shows a type glyph (PhotoWall.tsx:60, MediaThumb.tsx:68) â€” images silently vanish.
changes.fix: Combined with per-photo thumbnails (rank 2) pressure drops sharply. Additionally: make image GETs burst-tolerant / a higher separate limit for thumbnails vs full-file streams, and add long-lived caching so SW/browser serves repeats without re-hitting the proxy (extend the private max-age already on the redirect path to the stream/thumbnail paths).

changes.title: getProfile fetched twice per request (metadata + body) and never React-cached â†’ 2x getUser + 2x profile query
changes.evidence: generateMetadata calls getProfile (:19) and the page body calls it again (:41). getProfile is a plain server action, not React cache()-wrapped: each call runs supabase.auth.getUser() + a public_profiles select (profile-actions.ts:25-38). Next only dedupes native fetch(), not Supabase queries, so this is 2 profile lookups + 2 getUser round-trips. The body also does its own getUser (:39) â€” 3 getUser calls before content renders.
changes.fix: Wrap getProfile in React `cache()` so metadata and body share one result per request. Lift the page's own getUser into a cached helper too. Removes one profile query + two getUser round-trips per profile page load.

changes.title: Palace anchor wing-seal fan clipped mid-circle on phone (2-up anchor grid)
changes.evidence: WingFan renders up to 6 chips at 2.1rem with `marginLeft: i===0?0:"-0.45rem"` (:181) = ~10.35rem (166px). The anchors grid is `gridTemplateColumns: "1fr 1fr"` regardless of isMobile (:480), so at 360px each anchor is ~159px; content after `padding: "0.85rem 1rem 1rem"` (:229) is ~125px. changes.title: Subscription plan comparison collapses to one column on iPad portrait despite room for the 3-up grid
changes.evidence: Grid uses `(isMobile || isCompact) ? "1fr" : "repeat(3, 1fr)"` (:955), gap similarly (:956). iPad portrait is isCompact, so free/keeper/guardian stack into one column â€” long scroll, no side-by-side comparison â€” though an 834px viewport fits 3 cards (~250px each). The recommended-plan `transform: scale(1.03)` is also suppressed (:983). isCompact is being treated as "phone" on a tablet-wide viewport.

changes.title: Secondary tile titles truncate with ellipsis in the 2-column phone lane grid
changes.evidence: Lane grid `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(${isMobile?"8.5rem":"11rem"}, 1fr))` (:501). At 360px the tray inner ~293px â†’ two ~140px tiles. Inside a secondary tile the text span caps at `maxWidth: "68%"` (:300) and the title has WebkitLineClamp:2 + break-word (:301) at 1.0625rem â€” usable title box ~4rem. changes.title: iPad not a designed format: HomeView reserves 5.5rem top padding for a desktop top pill that doesn't exist on compact
changes.evidence: HomeView.tsx:190 only calls useIsMobile (no useIsCompact), so at 768-1024px the desktop branch runs: padding `isMobile ? "3rem 1rem calc(4.5rem + ...)" : "5.5rem 2.5rem 6rem"` (:818-820) with comment "top padding clears the floating NavigationBar pill" (:816-817). But NavigationBar renders the fixed BOTTOM bar on iPad (useMobileLayout, NavigationBar.tsx:314,:454,:480-484) â€” there is no top pill. Result: 5.5rem (plus scroll-container safe-area-top) of dead space above the greeting; bottom clearance works only by luck of the generic 6rem.

changes.title: Wing visit page has no top safe-area inset â€” breadcrumb sits under the notch/status bar
changes.evidence: Root `padding: isMobile ? "1rem 0.75rem 4rem" : "2rem 1rem 4rem"` â€” no env(safe-area-inset-top) anywhere. changes.title: jszip (244KB) ships on first paint of the security page though only needed on Export click

changes.title: Mobile settings-card override is dead code (selector space mismatch) â€” cards keep 2rem desktop side padding on phone
changes.evidence: Mobile style targets `.mp-settings-mobile-content > div > div[style*="border-radius: 1rem"]` (SPACE after colon). React serializes inline borderRadius:"1rem" to `border-radius:1rem` with NO space, so it never matches; the camelCase fallback selector never matches the kebab DOM attribute either. So the intended phone treatment (padding:1.125rem 1rem, radius:0.875rem, shadow:none) is never applied; cards keep desktop `padding:"1.75rem 2rem"` (profile/page.tsx:293,776,862,902,993 = 32px/side). With wrapper padding 1.25rem 1rem, a 360px phone loses 48px/side â†’ ~264px usable interior.
changes.fix: Fix the selector to match serialization: `div[style*="border-radius:1rem"]` (no space), drop the broken camelCase selector. Better: add a `stacked` prop to the card wrappers and set `padding: stacked ? "1.125rem 1rem" : "1.75rem 2rem"` inline.

changes.title: Toggle switches are 28px tall â€” below the 44px touch minimum for the 60+ audience
changes.evidence: Profile-visibility, AI-consent and daylight switches render `width:"3.25rem", height:"1.75rem"` (52x28px) at :565-566, 828-829, 1029-1030. The layout's mobile min-height bump explicitly excludes them: `.mp-settings-mobile-content button:not([role="switch"]) { min-height: 2.75rem }` (layout.tsx:395). So the tappable track is 28px tall vs the 44px target the brief requires.
changes.fix: Wrap each switch in a `minHeight:"2.75rem"` flex hit-area (pad the track vertically) or add transparent 2.75rem tap padding around the 52x28 track.

changes.title: iOS auto-zoom on focus: settings inputs stay 15px on iPad portrait â€” 16px override gated on isMobile only
changes.evidence: Base input is `fontSize: "0.9375rem"` = 15px (profile/page.tsx:1191). The 16px correction lives in a <style> gated `{isMobile && (` (layout.tsx:380) targeting `.mp-settings-mobile-content input`. iPad portrait is stacked but NOT isMobile, so it renders mp-settings-mobile-content yet never gets the bump â€” inputs stay 15px. iPad Safari/WKWebView auto-zooms on focus at <16px, shifting layout.
changes.fix: Change the gate from `{isMobile && (` to `{stacked && (` at :380 (the block already scopes to .mp-settings-mobile-content, only rendered when stacked). Or raise base inputStyle.fontSize to 1rem unconditionally.

changes.title: Me landing fixed at 38rem, never uses compact â€” actions don't stretch and float orphaned on iPad
changes.evidence: MeClient reads isCompact (:134) but stacked (:137) affects only top/bottom padding (:185-186). changes.title: Settings two-pane cramped in the 1025-1135px band â€” content can't reach its 46rem measure

changes.title: Me landing is a narrow 38rem column marooned in a full-width cream field on desktop/ultra-wide
changes.evidence: Board wrapper `maxWidth: "38rem", margin: "0 auto"` inside a `position: fixed; inset: 0` cream page (:180-189). changes.title: Settings toasts pinned to top:1.5rem ignore the notch â€” collide with the iOS status bar
changes.evidence: Toast `position: fixed, top: "1.5rem", right: "1.5rem"` with no safe-area inset; same in security/page.tsx:389, family/page.tsx:1010, connections/page.tsx:207. changes.title: Bottom-nav clearance reserves 3.5rem but the mobile bar is ~3.625rem+inset â€” last card row tucks under the bar
changes.evidence: Container reserves `calc(3.5rem + env(safe-area-inset-bottom,0px))` (:217-218). The fixed mobile bar height = tallest child = minHeight 2.75rem + padding 0.875rem = 3.625rem (NavigationBar.tsx:574-575) PLUS its own env(safe-area-inset-bottom) (:494). Canonical token is bottomBarH:"4rem" (theme.ts:65). So 3.5rem is ~0.125rem short of the bar and 0.5rem short of canon; the last card / 'Show More' sits partly under the nav hairline. Same under-reservation copied across Me/Settings/ProfilePageClient.
changes.fix: Reserve canonical height: `calc(4rem + env(safe-area-inset-bottom,0px))` (use T.layout.bottomBarH). Prefer fixing the shared convention across all call sites.

changes.title: Follow buttons on profile card and palace overview are ~2rem tall â€” under 2.75rem

changes.title: Secondary-tile descriptions and invite arrows are hover-only â€” permanently invisible on iPad touch
changes.evidence: The back-card carrying each secondary tile's desc is default-hidden (.relay-backcard opacity:0, :548) and only revealed inside `@media (hover: hover)` on hover/focus (:550-556); .relay-invite-arrow likewise (:549,:557-558). iPads report hover:none, so every compact tile in the three verb lanes shows only title + medallion â€” tile.desc ("Google Photos, iCloud & more", etc., HomeView.tsx:741-771) is unreachable. 15+ of ~20 lane tiles are secondary.

quickWins: ReactionBar.tsx:94, ProfileCard.tsx:150, PalaceOverviewClient.tsx:357, CommentThread.tsx:390/222, HomeView.tsx:667, AtriumRelay.tsx:404 â€” add minHeight:2.75rem + inline-flex to undersized touch targets (one-line each).
mobilePerf.ts:161 â€” flip loadBackgroundHDRI to false in MOBILE_QUALITY: one boolean, saves 6.5 MB on mobile 3D entry.
AtriumRelay.tsx:480 â€” `gridTemplateColumns: isMobile ? "1fr" : "1fr 1fr"` to stop the anchor seal-fan clipping.
settings/layout.tsx:380 â€” change `{isMobile && (` to `{stacked && (` to fix iPad input auto-zoom; :382 fix the border-radius selector (remove the space) to un-deadcode the mobile card padding.
subscription/page.tsx:955 â€” swap `(isMobile||isCompact)` for `isMobile` so iPad gets the 3-up plan grid.
Settings toasts (profile:251, security:389, family:1010, connections:207) â€” wrap top in calc(1.5rem + env(safe-area-inset-top)).
ExportPanel.tsx:6 â€” move `import JSZip` into the export click handler (drops 244KB from security first paint).
ipadVerdict: iPad is an accident, not a designed format. Only NavigationBar consults useIsCompact; HomeView, AtriumRelay, MeClient and the subscription grid never do. So iPad portrait renders the desktop branch of HomeView (5.5rem dead top band for a top pill that the bottom-bar nav removes), collapses the 3-up plan grid to one column as if it were a phone, leaves atrium tile descriptions hover-only and thus invisible, floats Me and its actions in a wide cream field, and keeps settings inputs at 15px so Safari auto-zooms on focus. The board content only 'works' by inheriting desktop grids (3-column lanes at 768px) â€” readable but by luck. Making iPad deliberate is cheap: add useIsCompact to HomeView's padding, gate the plan grid on isMobile, add a coarse/hover flag for tile descriptions, and flip the settings input gate to stacked.
perfVerdict: 1) Kill eager third-party/i18n JS on first paint: posthog-js (184KB, analytics.ts:1) and the full en.json (295KB, LandingV2Client.tsx:435) both ship before they're needed â€” dynamic-import both and jszip (244KB) behind its click. That's ~700KB off first paint across landing and settings, most of it never used pre-consent. 2) Fix the photo pipeline end-to-end: photos have no stored thumbnail (memoryStore.ts:218), so the Library wall pulls multi-MB originals per tile through a force-dynamic /api/media proxy capped at 200 req/min â€” which 429s and silently drops images on fast scroll. Generate+persist 280px photo thumbs on upload and backfill; the rate-limit pressure then largely evaporates. Public shares additionally 401 because next/image optimizes an auth-gated URL â€” return signed CDN URLs. 3) Stop paying 3D cost on 2D entry: warmPalaceScene mounts a WebGL context + full ExteriorScene graph + HDRI/PBR downloads on app mount (MemoryPalace.tsx:654 `hasVisitedPalace = true`) even for users who never open the palace, and mobile fetches a 6.5 MB background HDRI it's documented to skip (mobilePerf.ts:161). Gate the warm mount behind first 3D entry and flip the HDRI flag.
summary: This merges two audit passes into 33 fixable changes (P3 noise dropped), ranked with the highest-leverage perf wins first. The single biggest theme is wasted first-paint weight: three heavy libraries/data blobs (PostHog 184KB, the full English translation file 295KB, JSZip 244KB) all download on pages that don't use them yet, and the app boots a whole 3D scene even when you only open the flat Atrium or Library. The second theme is the photo pipeline â€” because uploaded photos never get a small thumbnail saved, every tile in the Library loads the full original through a proxy that rate-limits and starts silently dropping images when you scroll a big library; public share pages fail outright because they point image optimization at a login-only URL. The third theme is that iPad was never actually designed for â€” it inherits desktop layouts by accident, producing a dead band above the greeting, plan cards that stack into one column, atrium tile captions that are invisible on touch, and settings inputs small enough that Safari zooms in when you tap them. The fourth theme is touch targets: across the public visitor pages (reactions, follow, guestbook Post/Send, back links) and the Atrium, a lot of primary buttons are ~1.5-2rem tall, well under the 2.75rem minimum the 60+ audience needs â€” and many sit right next to correctly-sized siblings, so it's clearly an oversight. Most of these are one-to-three-line edits; the quickWins list calls out the ones worth doing this afternoon. Doing the seven perf/thumbnail items plus the iPad gating would meaningfully cut load time and finally make tablet a first-class format.
